## OI-140 — Whether the competition-adjusted ratio of talent available near this site may be computed

- ID: OI-140
- TYPE: CLOSED (was OPEN)
- NEEDED: The owner's answer: may the competition-adjusted ratio of the two-step floating catchment (PySAL `access`, BSD-3), the talent pool within reach over the competing demand within reach, be computed from the two released tables as an exception to PRV-30 and PRV-18 of [06_PRIVACY_AND_DISCLOSURE_CONTROL.md](docs/06_PRIVACY_AND_DISCLOSURE_CONTROL.md)?
- WHY: [Decision 0023](docs/decisions/0023-ten-additions-and-the-data-rule.md) item 1 first planned method card C39 with that ratio. The review of the decision's sweep found that the ratio divides one protected family by another, which PRV-30 does not allow, and reads the competing jobs on work units chosen by travel time instead of by the snap, which PRV-18 does not allow. AGENTS.md rule 12 forbids weakening a privacy invariant on the lead's authority, so the lead's ruling L-160 of 2026-11-14 recast card C39 and left the exception to the owner.
- DONE SO FAR: Card C39 shows two released figures side by side within 15, 30 and 45 minutes' drive: the talent pool (residents by occupation and pay band within reach) and the competing demand (jobs of the same occupations within reach). Each catchment snaps to whole release units, and PRV-18 and PRV-30 stay as they are. PRV-127 is a guard that refuses any ratio of the two figures; a planted ratio, a planted read on units chosen by travel time and a planted figure on an unsnapped outline each fail.
- OPTIONS: **Recommendation:** keep the two figures side by side, with no ratio. If the owner wants the ratio, a new decision record must amend PRV-30 and PRV-18. It must also say how the work units of the competing demand are chosen, because the release's unit-to-unit travel times hold `px_base` unit pairs only ([03_DATA_CONTRACTS.md](docs/03_DATA_CONTRACTS.md) DAT-153), and keep the rule that no choice of units depends on a protected value (PRV-19).
- NEEDED BY: task S6-T20; not a blocker, because the side-by-side form needs no exception.
- UPDATE: 2026-11-14, by the owner's answer of that day, recorded in [decision 0023](docs/decisions/0023-ten-additions-and-the-data-rule.md) item 1: yes. Card C39 keeps its two released figures side by side within 10, 20 and 30 minutes' drive and adds a third, qualified people within reach per competing job within reach, the quotient of those two released figures for the same occupation group and the same cut-off, shown to one decimal. It is computed only from the two released tables. It is the only exception to PRV-30 and PRV-18. PRV-127 refuses any other ratio of two protected families and any ratio computed before release. The two-step floating catchment is not used. Where an input is withheld the reason key is `ratio_input_withheld`; where no competing job is within reach the reason key is `no_competing_jobs`.
- CLOSED: 2026-11-14, by the owner's answer, recorded in decision 0023 item 1. The earlier text is kept.

Its gateway outcomes are 176 DECIDED and 84 BELOW_THRESHOLD, and two decided cases are wrong (A-M-048 and A-M-049). The cause is not found. No test, wait, bound or retry was changed.
- OPTIONS: **Default:** task S2-T10, which holds the criterion on the suite's time (OI-158), repeats the standalone browser run on four processors with the browser's log and the page's console kept on a failure of readiness, and records either the cause or the number of runs without the failure; no retry is added to the test and no bound moves before the cause is known.
- NEEDED BY: the slice S2 gate (task S2-T10).
- UPDATE: 2026-11-14, by the second round of the slice S1 gate record: a likely cause is found, and the item stays open. By the browser tool's own report the failing run started at 17:18:31, and the test failed about one second into it. In that second, four campaigns of the mutation tester, started by a builder's job at 17:17:19, were running in the shared process-number space of the build machine, and three of them recorded time-outs that fired. The tester sends its time-out signal to a process number that may by then belong to another process (OI-168), and a browser process that is stopped in that way gives this message. No record says which process ended, so the cause is not proved. The default stands, now with no campaign in the shared space: the repeated standalone run of task S2-T10 either shows the failure again or counts the runs without it.

- INVESTIGATION (2026-11-20, S2-T10 package P02): LEFT OPEN. The recorded page closure at 17:18:31 on 2026-11-14 overlaps the four campaigns started at 17:17:19, but no record identifies the signalled process; that remains a hypothesis, not a cause. The test-only page helper now retains console, pageerror, crash, close and browser-disconnected events from before navigation through readiness and prints them only on readiness rejection. Its planted tests fail without reporting and pass with it, including an unchanged host-deadline plant; exact red/green exits and standalone-run counts are in PROGRESS.md, “S2-T10 P02 — Random-failure diagnosis records”. Those passes do not reconstruct the missing historical browser log. No wait, retry or bound changes; a future matching failure still needs its browser/process evidence.

- CORRECTION (2026-11-20, S2-T10 package P02 review r1, F1/F2/F3): LEFT OPEN. The new invented-page test calls open() itself, keeps the navigation pageerror as the first reported event, preserves the original readiness rejection and checks that diagnostic listener counts return to zero. Its pre-navigation registration no-op plant exits 1 and restoration exits 0. Rejected navigation now reports retained events once and rethrows the original rejection; the foreign-request path checks settled after goto and abandons readiness. The corresponding invented cases fail before these two changes and pass after them. By code reading (open() disposes its logger when the foreign plant wins, and ready() then registers a new one after navigation), these are teardown of pending readiness promises, not a recurrence of the unexplained smoke failure; see review finding F2. This describes the earlier implementation; the F2 guard now prevents that late ready() call. Commands and real exits: PROGRESS.md, “S2-T10 P02 — Review r1 corrections”. No historical cause or closure is claimed.
- CLARIFICATION (2026-11-20, review r1 confirmation of package P02, note N1): in the preceding correction row, 'these' means the two `close` events printed as READINESS FAILURE before the passing foreign-asset tests in the earlier P02 runs (PROGRESS.md, 'S2-T10 P02 — Random-failure diagnosis records'), not the invented cases.

## OI-168 — The mutation tester's time-out can stop a process that is not its own

- ID: OI-168
- TYPE: CLOSED
- NEEDED: A way to run `scripts/mutation.py` that cannot stop a process outside its own campaign.
- WHY: The pinned mutation tester (mutmut, the dependency group `mutation`) records a deadline and a process number for every mutant run and cancels no entry when a run ends. When a deadline passes, it sends the signal SIGXCPU to that number (its module `mutmut/workers/timeout.py`, whose own comment says that entries of ended processes stay until they reach the top). On a machine that reuses process numbers quickly, the number can by then belong to another process of the same user, which ends with "CPU time limit exceeded" (exit code 152). On 2026-11-14 a run of the guard-test discovery on the build machine ended that way within a minute, while a builder's campaign ran in the same process-number space; the same command at the same commit passed once no such campaign ran. The highest process number of the build machine is 99999. A random failure and its cause are recorded (AGENTS rule 39).
- DONE SO FAR: The lead read the tester's module in full and found no limit on processor time in any shell, script or test of the repository. The campaign was stopped, and since then every campaign on the build machine is started in a process-number space of its own, with the sandbox tool the repository already uses, where it can reach only its own processes. Nothing in the repository is changed. The stopped run was not a run of the slice S1 gate. The lead's run records were read for the three random failures recorded earlier: OI-163 falls in a second in which four such campaigns were running (the update in that item); OI-125 and OI-160 do not fall on a campaign. The web mutation runner uses another tool, which was not examined.
- OPTIONS: **Default:** `scripts/mutation.py` starts the tester in a process-number space of its own and refuses to run where it cannot, with a planted case; no fallback to the shared space. Alternative: raise the pin once the tester cancels its entries, and keep the separate space until then.
- NEEDED BY: task S2-T10; until then no campaign runs in the shared process-number space of the build machine.
- RESOLUTION: 2026-11-17, S2-T10 part A. All tester launch paths in scripts/mutation.py (local run/show and pilot discovery/run) now use a private process namespace. The inner check refuses a shared namespace and an unavailable launcher returns failure without fallback. The live subprocess probe and planted omitted-isolation and missing-launcher cases pass. No mutation campaign was run in part A.

## OI-129 — One sandbox timing test failed once under machine load

- ID: OI-129
- TYPE: CLOSED (was OPEN), 2026-11-20, by the fix of task S2-T10 part F in merge train S2-9.
- NEEDED: The cause of one failure of `test_die_with_parent` in `scripts/tests/test_sandbox_mounts.py`, or a record that it did not recur over a stated number of runs.
- WHY: AGENTS.md rule 39: a random failure is recorded, and a green re-run alone does not close it.
- DONE SO FAR: During task S2-T01 (2026-11-13), the builder's whole test run at seed 2026111377 failed this test once with "a sandboxed process outlived its driver", while the machine was loaded (a load average of 74 on 32 processors, ruling L-106 of the run). The same test passed in the lead's whole runs at seeds 2026111378 and 2026111382, which ran at lower priority and finished with 0 failed. In the same builder run, two tests of the version check failed because that tool's shell had Node 24 first on its path instead of the pinned 22; that is an environment fault and not a random failure, and the lead's runs with Node 22 passed. No code was changed because of either.
- OPTIONS: **Recommendation:** count the failures of this test over the next ten local runs and record the count here; if it recurs, make the test wait for the process group to end for a stated time before it judges, never loosen the assertion that the process does not outlive its driver.
- NEEDED BY: the slice S2 gate.
- CLOSED BY: the cause was found and fixed, not a re-run. When the driver was killed while bubblewrap was starting, the inner bubblewrap had not yet armed its parent-death signal and outlived the driver with the sandboxed process; under CPU contention `test_die_with_parent` failed 5 to 7 of 30 runs. Task S2-T10 part F adds a child subreaper between the launcher and bubblewrap (`scripts/sandbox_supervisor.py`) and bounds the stalled-run cleanup by one deadline; a deterministic reproduction fails on the base and passes on the fix, and `test_die_with_parent` is unchanged. Five commits, each reviewed or confirmed by another maker; the evidence and verdicts are in PROGRESS.md under the headings "S2-T10 part F". The assumptions the reviews left open are OI-351 and OI-352.

## OI-170 — The `Employed` indicator of the municipal population source is not loaded

- ID: OI-170
- TYPE: OPEN
- NEEDED: the privacy judgement whether a count of the employed by municipality of residence belongs in what the attacker is assumed to know, taken at the design of slice S5; until then the count stays unloaded.
- WHY: the source `pop_muni` holds an `Employed` indicator that maps to no contract token of `pub_population_municipality`; whether such a count is part of the attacker's assumed knowledge is a privacy judgement, not a mapping the task may choose (the lead's ruling for the seventh pass).
- DONE SO FAR: `custodian/publicdata/review/population_indicators.csv` lists `Employed` with a blank token; the live build reports the unmapped indicators' rows as not loaded (192 rows on the real run, `Employed` among them), refuses an indicator the file does not list with the source and the indicator named, and a test pins the committed file with two planted edits of a copy.
- OPTIONS: **Recommendation:** decide at the slice S5 privacy design, before any task loads or uses the count; loading it earlier needs that decision first.
- NEEDED BY: the design of slice S5.
- UPDATE: 2026-11-19, by [decision 0064](docs/decisions/0064-the-narrowing-rows-decided.md) item 15: the owner restores the indicator. S2-T38 loads it as a Public fact on the source's own geography, with source and year, never joined to a synthetic record, used to segment one, apportioned to a drawn area or combined with a protected figure (rule 10). The item stays open only for how the attack model of slice S5 counts the published figure, a point of S5's privacy design in which no privacy rule, attack size or tolerance is relaxed (rule 12).
- UPDATE: 2026-11-19, by S2-T38: `custodian/publicdata/review/population_indicators.csv` maps `Employed` to the token `employed`, unit `persons`, admitted in `pub_population_municipality` only (`TABLE_UNITS` of `frame/census.py`); the other three census tables refuse it. It is not `employees`/`persons` and is not one of the four audit-count pairs of PUB-84 and DAT-128 (`UNITS` is unchanged and pinned with a planted fifth pair), so it is no audit selector. Document 03 lists it in the 7.3 row of the table and in DAT-128. For S5's privacy design: the attack model counts the published figure either as `not_applicable` with one closed PRV-115 reason, or as `enabled` after a release-contract revision that lists the pair with its stated relation (`equal`, `upper` or `lower`); until then DAT-128's strict default holds, and a count found applicable fails the privacy build. No privacy rule, attack size, tolerance or audit selector changed. Every later consumer of the rows routes through `validate_employed_use` of `frame/population.py`, which admits Public display on the source's geography only and refuses joins, segmentation, apportionment, invented geography, protected composites, movement anchors and the reserved grid use, each with a planted test; no consumer calls it yet.

  - D1, an exact half can round the wrong way, and the identity of MTH-21 is not exact (functions `ratio`, `weighted_mean` and `decomposition`): division is made at 28 digits before the later steps, so the value handed to `rounded` is already rounded once. A breach of "round only at the end" (document 04 section 10).

Invented input: three named months of 42, 9 and 8, one other month of 2, 4 in June 2025, 6 in December 2014 and 9 undated. Got a dated total of 71 and a share of 83; expected the calendar's own total and share, 61 and 97, with the outside rows counted apart, or a refusal that names the period.
  - D5, a sum of quantities whose unit the source does not state (`country_totals` of the figures module; an internal evidence file only). Invented input: two rows of one country with quantities 3 and 40. Got a quantity of 43; expected no such total (PUB-45: other units are counted, never combined).

Two explained causes of an exit 1 of this suite are on record for other runs and are not shown to be the cause here: the interrupt test under a launch that ignores the interrupt signal (PO-S2-06), and, in a later pass of another task in another tool's sandbox, the two version tests failing because that sandbox's Node was outside the pinned line. ## OI-254 — A test that copied the user's uv cache filled the temporary folder held in memory

- ID: OI-254
- TYPE: RANDOM FAILURE (environment)
- NEEDED: A guard that no test copies the whole user uv cache, beyond the bounded seed of the clean-installation test.
- WHY: On 2026-11-15 at 23:43 the build machine's temporary folder (a 48 GB file system held in memory) filled, and on 2026-11-16 the lead's ledger run of this task met the same error. The cause was this task's own cache seed in `scripts/tests/test_clean_environment.py`, carried into the joined S3-T06 tree: it copied the whole user uv cache into each child cache; across file systems the hard link failed, every symbolic link was followed and hard-linked files were copied once per name, so a 1.5 GB cache became about 5.3 GB per child cache, and the file held about eight at once. Seven cases failed with error 28 (no space left), and two unrelated mutation campaigns on the same machine died of the same full disk.
- DONE SO FAR: Fix pass 4 of this task: child caches keep symbolic and hard links, the user cache is copied at most once per run of the file and every further child cache is made by links; a new test with a planted plain copy proves it, and the lead measured the peak use of the temporary folder against the bound. S3-T06 and S3-T02 drop their own versions of the file at their re-cuts. The lead's mutation campaigns keep their temporary folder on the main disk. A limit found (2026-11-16, at fix pass 5): with no temporary folder set, Python uses the memory-backed `/tmp`, and the one class copy of a large user cache (about 22 GB apparent on the build machine) fails there with error 28 because the file system's table of 1,048,576 file entries runs out, not its bytes. The lead's ledger and head checks set the temporary folder on the disk that holds the cache, where the seed links instead of copying; the hosted tests job's cache is about 0.5 GB.
- OPTIONS: **Default:** keep the bounded seed; a later task may add a planted-violation check that a test's temporary copies stay under a size bound.
- NEEDED BY: Before the next joined whole test on the build machine.

### PO-S2-23 — The browser's rendering threads choose their own processors

- ID: PO-S2-23
- TYPE: OPEN
- RAISED BY: the lead's measurement of 2026-11-15, entered with S1-T18
- CONCERNS: AGENTS.md rule 44 (a timeout is replayed alone at normal load); any run whose result is a time
- EVIDENCE: The headless browser of the browser tests, started inside a run bound to a set of processors, keeps its own process on that set, but its sixteen rendering threads hold processors 0 to 11: the renderer sets its threads' processors itself, and a set given from outside does not bind them. A browser suite therefore loads processors 0 to 11 whatever set its run was given, and a timed run beside it is not clean. Nothing in the repository is changed; binding those threads would need a system setting that is the owner's.
- NEEDED: the follow-up task of slice S2 looks at the renderer's own thread options. Until then the lead takes a run whose result is a time only while no browser suite is in flight, and replays a timed-out mutant or a time-limit failure seen beside a browser suite after that suite has ended, keeping both results.

- INVESTIGATION (2026-11-20, S2-T10 package P02): LEFT OPEN; no launch argument adopted. Read the official [Run Chromium with command-line switches](https://www.chromium.org/developers/how-tos/run-chromium-with-flags/), [cc/base/switches.cc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/cc/base/switches.cc) and [content/public/common/content_switches.cc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/content/public/common/content_switches.cc), retrieved 2026-11-20. Their documented meanings distinguish raster-task thread count (num-raster-threads), renderer-process count (renderer-process-limit), and a renderer command prefix (renderer-cmd-prefix). Inference: those descriptions do not establish per-thread processor confinement for the pinned headless shell, and current upstream source is not a runtime proof for that shell. No setting, sandbox or rendering mode is changed. The existing rule to separate timed runs from browser suites stands. Needed: an owned per-thread affinity probe and deciding control-on/control-off evidence on the actual pinned shell; normal and loaded test passes are not that proof.

### PO-S2-69 — The invented boundary archive followed the clock, so one frame test failed at random

- ID: PO-S2-69
- TYPE: RANDOM FAILURE
- RAISED BY: the lead (Anthropic Claude), 2026-11-16, from the clean test run of a local mutation campaign of task S4-T03
- CONCERNS: `custodian/tests/fixtures/frame/invented.py` (`invented_archive`); `custodian/tests/test_frame_live_survivors.py` (`test_bnd_hdx_receipt_is_kept_under_that_source_id`)
- EVIDENCE: The mutation tester's clean run failed once: 1 failed, 1,510 passed; the test compared the receipt's hash of the archive built inside the world with the hash of a second build in its assertion, and the two differed. The same test passed alone (13 passed). Cause: `invented_archive` wrote each member with `ZipFile.writestr(name, ...)`, which stamps the member with the current local time, so two builds on either side of a two-second step of the zip time give different bytes; two builds 2.1 seconds apart were reproduced with different hashes.
- RESOLUTION: the fixture writes each member with a fixed member time and the same permission bits, and the planted test `custodian/tests/test_frame_fixture_archive.py::test_invented_archive_bytes_do_not_follow_the_clock` builds the archive at two clock readings an hour apart and requires one hash; it failed before the fix and passes after it. This closes the item by a found cause, not by a green re-run (rule 39). The inline archive of `custodian/tests/test_frame_coverage.py` is built and read once per test and is not hashed twice; it is left unchanged.

## OI-314 — The unstable-key evidence test fails for some string hash seeds

- ID: OI-314
- TYPE: OPEN
- RAISED BY: the lead's ruling L-1050 of 2026-11-19, from the random failure of the S2-T37 whole run (seed 3764211809)
- CONCERNS: `custodian/tests/test_investment_evidence_survivors_8.py::test_unstable_caller_key_never_invents_identifier_text`; AGENTS.md rules 36, 37 and 39; task S2-T40
- EVIDENCE: The test failed alone under `PYTHONHASHSEED=3764211809` (its `project_key` case) and under `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` (two `project_id` cases), and passed under 0; the whole-test runner passes the run seed as `PYTHONHASHSEED`, so the failure was deterministic per seed. Cause: the test's `missing_on` pins one global index into the equality calls on the caller-supplied unstable key, but the count and order of those calls follow the row dict's slot layout, which the string hash seed sets. A field lookup crosses the unstable key's slot for some layouts only, and one lookup can compare the stored key more than once after a not-equal result, so the failing comparison lands on a different field lookup per seed (under seed 0 the `project_id` order is `receipt-metadata check`, `archived-parser comparison`, `current-set lookup`, `revision-loop lookup`; under seed 1 the same fixed lookups consume five comparisons, the `current-set lookup` comparing the key twice). Production code performs its lookups in a fixed order and iterates no set or dict of string keys in a seed-dependent order that reaches an equality call; the test assumed one order.
- NEEDED: Task S2-T40 fixes the test at that cause, so it states its property for every order of the unstable key's comparisons (a missing identity part stays empty and never becomes invented text; the control and the second revision keep their exact equalities; the only other outcome is the receipt-metadata refusal) and a guard runs it under a fixed list of hash seeds in subprocesses. The item closes when S2-T40 merges; a green re-run under one seed alone never closes it (rule 39).



## OI-323 — The dev-server entry transform exceeded a single request timeout

- ID: OI-323
- TYPE: OPEN, cause fixed locally; independent confirmation and merged-result evidence pending.
- RAISED BY: S2-T42, from the lead's TRAIN-S2-5.head1 failure record of 2026-11-19 (also identified there as proposed item PO-S2-115).
- CONCERNS: `web/scripts/check-dev-server.mjs`, `web/scripts/tests/check-dev-server.node-test.mjs`; AGENTS.md rules 36, 37 and 39.
- EVIDENCE: `.overnight/IN/HEAD1-FAILURE.md` records whole-test exit 1, 11662 passed and one failed, with `real shell starts` reporting an internal TIMEOUT under load. At base `55657e59d80098d9860d3a8463431cd33bdf45a7`, `run` fetches the entry once through `httpGet` with `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` and no `isNotYet` catch; `poll` handles those transient errors for the page only. The injected-clock regression leaves that production code unchanged and reproduces `FAIL internal-error: TIMEOUT: timed out` (one failed test, exit 1, `.overnight/tmp/red.log`).
- CAUSE: The single entry request's one-second limit becomes an internal error if the first transform outlasts it. The recorded machine-load explanation is consistent with this code path; this worker did not independently measure the historical transform duration.
- FIX: S2-T42 runs both requests through the same polling function and startup deadline, bounds requests and pauses by the remaining startup and outer budgets, retries only the existing not-yet errors, and names the entry URL on startup expiry. Virtual-clock plants cover delayed success, a never-answering entry, immediate 404 and wrong-content-type failures, other errors, shared-budget expiry and the outer bound. Four temporary source violations each produce exit 1 and are removed; commands and final checks are appended in PROGRESS.md under S2-T42.
- NEEDED: Another maker confirms the task's local result; the lead supplies the hosted and exact-merge whole-test evidence before recording closure. A green rerun alone does not close this random failure. OI-323 follows the highest ID on the brief's supplied base; local main/origin tracking refs are older, and the lead may renumber at the join if needed.
- NEEDED BY: S2-T42 review and the slice S2 gate.

## S2-18-RF1 — Hosted timing failure of one section 10 property test (2026-11-22, lead)

Random failure, recorded under rule 39. The hosted "Run all tests" job of 2026-11-22 on train S2-18 head `8f75f027a1` failed one test: `custodian/tests/test_assembly_section10.py::test_final_audit_refuses_exactly_a_mismatch_or_an_unrecorded_figure`, with Hypothesis `DeadlineExceeded` (273 ms against the 200 ms default) on the all-absent case. The other 15184 tests passed. Cause: each example runs a full final audit, which parses the 1.2 MB source registry. Locally the runtime is up to 195 ms on a dedicated core, so the test sits at the timer's edge. Disposition: the domain is finite (4 × 3 × 3 = 36 states), so the test now enumerates all of it with `pytest.mark.parametrize` and has no per-example timer. This is exhaustive, so it is a stronger test than a sample, with no assertion change. The same class was handled for the tender tests under PO-S2-P46-03. A green rerun alone did not close this item; it closes when the train merges with the change.

- ID: OI-414
- TYPE: OPEN
- RAISED BY: S2-P100 fx1 (Cognition Devin), 2026-11-24, under ruling L-1861.
- CONCERNS: three of the 54 agency copies have no `pub_investqa_page` row by the release check of [decision 0029](docs/decisions/0029-the-agencys-pages-as-verbatim-quotations.md) item 5, each on genuine visible page text: `ar15` (`/ar/sectors-and-opportunities/financial-services`) and `en15` (`/en/sectors-and-opportunities/financial-services`) are refused `page_contact_shape` because their own "what's happening" text publishes an e-mail-shaped contact token; `ar18` (`/ar/sectors-and-opportunities/manufacturing`) is refused `page_contact_shape` because the same region publishes `2024-2030`, a hyphenated year range the telephone-number shape fuses as an eight-digit run. The pages' typed `pub_investqa_record` rows still show with their links, and the quotation shows the missing-page state of decision 0029 item 4.
- WHY: the check does exactly what the record says — a page whose text holds a contact-shaped token has no row, and verbatim admits no redaction; under `investqa_page_text@1` these pages passed only through the extraction defect that `@2` removed, so this is the protection rule applied to the true page text, not a value cut. The check is not weakened and no exemption is made.
- DONE SO FAR: the refusals are recorded by the b1 evidence re-run (`.overnight/IN/B1-RETURN.md`: 3 of 54 copies refused `page_contact_shape`, 51 `page_text` rows written); `language_confirmation.ar` in `custodian/publicdata/investment_pages.yaml` sets the fields the evidence supports and leaves `field_coverage_recorded` and `live_page_compared` false for these no-row pages.
- RECORDED, NOT BUILT: the ar18 refusal is a false positive of the phone shape — the en18 twin's `2024–2030` uses an en dash and passes. It is a possible later record only: any change to the shape scan needs its own decision record with planted cases; nothing is built for it.
- NEEDED BY: the slice S2 gate record; any later review of the contact scan.
- UPDATE, 2026-11-25, S2-T39B b1: the owner's "option b" is recorded as Proposed [decision 0120](docs/decisions/0120-year-range-is-not-a-phone-shape.md) and Proposed [decision 0121](docs/decisions/0121-agency-pages-box-1-covers-pages-that-pass-the-release-check.md). This supersedes the earlier "nothing is built" status for the year-range reading only: the exact ascending ASCII year-range exception has invented-fixture tests, and `ar18` is expected to pass once the lead reruns the real evidence. `ar15` and `en15` remain refused `page_contact_shape` for their e-mail shapes and keep their typed records and links. Box 1 covers passing pages under proposed decision 0121; `field_coverage_recorded` and `live_page_compared` read over stored pages but remain false until that rerun. No saved page was read by this workspace task and no refusal is closed on invented-fixture evidence.
